jobs.title: Drift Wood #32 · the red pen
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, chin up, unkempt dark hair falling forward, sharp jaw; CHLOE — aged 19, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders. WOOD usually wears oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn even indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers. CHLOE wears mazzy star hoodie. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Chloe proofs the drawing, not the text. Seattle, said sideways. Panel 1: two teenagers at desks pushed together in a dark school newsroom under one desk lamp, a boy inking a comic page, a girl with heavy eyeliner marking his drawing with a red pen, black window behind (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE). Chloe says "Your cashier has six fingers.". Wood says "It's expressive.". Panel 2: over-the-shoulder close-up of a red pen circling a crudely drawn six-fingered hand on a comic page under lamp light (in this panel: CHLOE, WOOD). Chloe says "It's a sixth finger.". Wood says "Egon Schiele—". Chloe says "—had the correct number of fingers and drew them wrong on purpose. You drew this one wrong by accident and now you're citing Vienna.". Panel 3: a teenage boy at a desk deliberately adding another finger to a drawing while a girl beside him watches unreadably, desk lamp, deep black shadows (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 4: wide shot of two desks pushed together in a dark newsroom, two teenagers with heads down and pens moving, a large black window taking up most of the frame, one small lamp (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE). Chloe says "I'm going to Seattle.". Wood says "I know.". Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized crab, seen from above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
